_about: The 1900 Materials' review keyboard, replacing the workspace's (jesup/config/keyboard.json, the Latin notation of The Chukchee) whole. Phonetic, for an editor who has no Russian keyboard and reads no Russian: a Latin key types the Cyrillic letter nearest its sound, shift its capital, and the keys a Latin alphabet has no letter for carry the rest, one keystroke each and no dead keys. Every button in the panel shows its key. Kbd mode (ctrl-space) is off by default, so ASCII punctuation stays typeable in prose. Comma, period, hyphen, space and 9 are never bound.
_keys: Letters: a а, b б, v в, g г, d д, e е, z з, i и, j й, k к, l л, m м, n н, o о, p п, r р, s с, t т, u у, f ф, h х, c ц, y ы, x ж, w ш, q я. The rest of the Russian alphabet: semicolon ч, [ щ, ] ю, \ э, / ь, and question mark ъ. The pre-1918 letters: = і, 0 ѣ, 8 ѳ, shifted for the capital. The notation's letters (config/keying.json inventory) on the digits, shifted for the capital: 1 ӄ, 2 ӈ, 3 ђ, 4 һ, 5 ѵ, 6 ð, 7 ł. The marks are postfix, attaching to the letter before the caret as the corpus's NFD stores them: ' acute and ` grave, as The Chukchee's stress key is ', " diaeresis (ӓ is а then "), ~ breve (ў is у then ~; й has its own key), < cedilla (с̧ is с then <), > circumflex (а̂ is а then >, 1-024 l22, 1-025 l7), _ caron (р̌ is р then _, 1-036; ј̌ is ј then _, 1-114 l24 — the editor could not type it before this key). The letters with no key of their own — ј, є, the tall l and w, which the layers key Latin — are palette buttons: every letter key is taken, and ( is needed in prose for every (стр. N).
_palette: Every letter the book's Russian and its notation use, as buttons, so a letter is reachable by its shape without knowing its key.
